advances: The planar stable-arc second-order stress with actual moving cap coordinates, without cap-quantile smoothness. It does not produce such an arc or a buffered weighted continuation.

proof:
Choose admissible preimages of a basis of the finite-dimensional image $(U_z)_z$. Taking their linear combinations realizes every acceleration coordinate by actual compactly supported signed arc changes. The linear cap constraints preserve the exact full-plane covers: the continuous part stays balanced, active margins do not fall, and finitely many strict margins persist. Smooth compactly supported changes in $L$ preserve the active rows exactly, and positive curvature and strict compatibility gaps on their supports ensure feasibility for small parameters of either sign.

For each $v\in L$, choose a nonzero smooth function $\phi$ supported in a short compact interval of $I$ of length less than $\pi$, orthogonal to every $r_z$. Such a function exists by taking more disjoint smooth bumps than there are linear equations. The Dirichlet inequality gives $\int(\phi^2-\phi'^2)<0$; rescale to make this $-1$. The planar support area formula and strict cap localization (6ae2eb173ed91aee) show that $v\phi$ has all first fiber and cap masses zero and joint second mass vector $B(v)=(-\sum_z v_z^2,(-\sum_z I_{jz}v_z^2)_j)$. Finite nonnegative combinations of these vectors are realized by choosing disjoint short supports and multiplying by square roots of their coefficients. Quadratic cross terms then vanish. Call the resulting perturbation $\delta h$ and its second mass vector $B$.

For any acceleration $a\in A$, take the arc path $h+t\delta h+(t^2/2)\psi$, homothety factor $1+(t^2/2)\kappa$, and affine cap motion at size $s=t^2/2$. Pulling back the homothety changes the old cap margin by $s\ell_j+O(s^2)$ uniformly on the bounded fibers. Apply the fixed-body slicing proof (4)–(5) of 6b80e85ff6937910 with density velocity zero and divide by $\|u_j\|$ for the unnormalized plane: proper sections contribute $\ell_j$, inside supporting edges $\min(0,\ell_j)$, and outside supporting edges $\max(0,\ell_j)$ before this division. An $O(s^2)$ margin error affects mass by $O(s^2)$ by the same bounded-slice estimate. Finite section moments of the bounded edge subdensities make $G_j$ compact convex. One sign indicator on each edge realizes its derivative contribution, so the actual acceleration derivative $D_j(a)$ is a value of a form in $G_j$, and in particular is bounded by its support function. The arc changes are localized on a common compact guard strictly separated from every cap plane, so for all sufficiently small $t$ their exact volume contribution to each moved cap is its inside bit times the full arc area change, by the boundary localization of 6ae2eb173ed91aee. Thus mass and cap masses have expansions $M+s(B_0+L_0(a))+o(s)$ and $D+s(B_j+D_j(a))+o(s)$. The body and cover feasibility just checked apply to the combined path.

There can be no $B,a$ with $B_0+L_0(a)>0$ and all $B_j+\sup_{G_j}g(a)<0$, since the moving covers with persistent slack would yield depth below $\beta$. The convex cone of all vectors with $x_0\le B_0+L_0(a)$ and $x_j\ge B_j+\sup_{G_j}g(a)$ therefore avoids the open cone $x_0>0,\ x_j<0$. Separate from the open cone to obtain a nonzero functional $-\alpha_0 x_0+\sum_j\lambda_jx_j$ nonnegative on the former cone, with all displayed coefficients nonnegative. In the signed joint homothety direction $\kappa=1,\psi=0,\delta u_j=0,\delta v_j=v_j,\delta b_j=b_j$, the relative margin derivative vanishes on every old section. Thus $L_0=2M$ and each cap form is $2D$, with their negatives on the opposite feasible direction. With $B=0$, these tests force $\alpha_0 M=D\sum_j\lambda_j$ and $\alpha_0>0$. Normalize $\alpha_0=1$. Testing $B(v)$ gives the quadratic inequality; testing both signs of arc accelerations gives the claimed equality because all cap forms agree there. With $\psi_z=v_z\phi$ and arbitrary compact smooth $\phi$ this equality gives $\sum_zW_z v_z r_z(\theta)=0$. Applying $1+\partial_\theta^2$ to the active rows gives $r(\theta)\in L$, hence the stated nullspace conclusion.

Finally put $G=\sum_j\lambda_jG_j$. The separation inequality with $B=0$ says $\sup_{g\in G}(g-L_0)(a)\ge0$ for every $a\in A$. If the compact convex $G$ missed the closed convex $L_0+A^*$, strict separation would give a direction in $A$ with the opposite strict inequality (the dual of $A^*$ is the closed cone $A$). Hence a single choice of the consistent allocated forms has the asserted joint property.

statement:
Let a compatible finite positive planar fiber family be a local minimum of maximum normalized ambient closed-halfspace depth in the fiber Hausdorff topology, with value $\beta>0$, total area $M$ and raw budget $D=\beta M$. Choose finite exact critical positive circuit groups at the deepest bases, and fixed strictly cheaper full-plane covers elsewhere. A critical cap $j$ has margin $u_j\cdot x+v_j\cdot z-b_j$, $u_j\ne0$, and area $D$. Each group has fixed positive coefficients $\rho_j$ with $\sum_j\rho_ju_j=0$ and assigned bases with nonnegative weighted constant margin.

On an open support-normal interval $I$ assume $h_z$ is $C^2$, $r_z=h_z+h_z''>0$, the same finite compatibility rows vanish identically with kernel $L$, and all other rows have positive gaps on the compact subintervals used. For every cap and fiber the exposed boundary on $I$ stays on a fixed strict side, with a positive uniform gap on compact subintervals. Write $I_{jz}$ for its inside bit. Take any signed smooth compactly supported $L$-valued support acceleration $\psi$, signed common homothety speed $\kappa$, and cap speeds $(\delta u_j,\delta v_j,\delta b_j)$ preserving $\sum_j\rho_j\delta u_j=0$ and satisfying $\sum_j\rho_j(\delta v_j\cdot z-\delta b_j)\ge0$ at the assigned bases with zero old weighted margin. Let $A$ be their acceleration cone, representing $\psi$ by the finite vector $(U_z)_z$ with $U_z=\int_I\psi_z r_z\,d\theta$. Put $L_0=2\kappa M+\sum_z U_z$. Let $G_j$ be the set of linear forms on these coordinates with fixed term $2\kappa D+\sum_z I_{jz}U_z$, proper-section term $\int\ell_j/\|u_j\|\,d\mathcal H^1$, and on each coincident supporting edge a term $\int\alpha\ell_j/\|u_j\|\,d\mathcal H^1$ with one arbitrary Borel $0\le\alpha\le1$, where $\ell_j=\delta u_j\cdot x+\kappa u_j\cdot x+\delta v_j\cdot z-\delta b_j$.

There is a single vector $\lambda_j\ge0$ with $\sum_j\lambda_j=1/\beta$ such that $W_z=1-\sum_j\lambda_j I_{jz}$ satisfies
$$
\sum_zW_z v_z^2\ge0\ (v\in L),\qquad
\sum_zW_z\int_I\psi_z r_z\,d\theta=0
$$
for every such $\psi$. In particular $r(\theta)$ belongs to the nullspace of the diagonal form restricted to $L$ for every $\theta\in I$. For the same $\lambda_j$ one can choose one $g_j\in G_j$ per cap with $\sum_j\lambda_jg_j-L_0$ nonnegative on $A$. No differentiable cap quantiles are required.
title: Direct planar cap budgets give one curvature stress with moving cap coordinates
